title: NimbusCompute + Redwood Partner Discovery

Action items assigned for deck, pricing template, and technical onboarding checklist.

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan, Samir Patel (Redwood); Rachel Lee, Marco Diaz, Irene Cho (NimbusCompute)

Summary (auto): quick partner intro, explore GTM and integration models, identify security checkpoints and pilot scope.

[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, happy to kick off, I'm Alex, I'm the AE on the Redwood Partnerships team. Samir, do you want to intro?
[00:12] Samir Patel: Yeah hi all, Samir here, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll cover the tech bits. Rachel, Marco, Irene, thanks for taking time.
[00:20] Rachel Lee: Thanks Alex, excited to talk, we've been hunting for a solid inference platform partner to offer capacity and a marketplace integration.
[00:30] Marco Diaz: Hi, Marco here on partnerships and channel, curious on commercial models, resale, revenue share, etc.
[00:38] Irene Cho: Irene, I'm the systems eng, I'll be the technical contact. We run a mix of A100 and H100 clusters, also some AMD MI300 in lab.
[00:50] Alex Morgan: Great, that mix is helpful. High-level goal for today's call: quick intros, figure out partnership models that make sense, and identify blockers for a pilot.
[01:05] Samir Patel: On the technical side we want to understand how you surface capacity — is it via marketplace listing that customers can 1-click, or are you thinking a dedicated resale where Nimbus resells dedicated Redwood capacity?
[01:22] Rachel Lee: We actually want both options, ideally. Some customers prefer MSP-managed dedicated GPU pools, others want to consume via a marketplace with BYO options.
[01:34] Marco Diaz: From channel side, the revenue share is huge; we'd prefer a carve-out for reseller but open to referral for smaller deals.
[01:43] Alex Morgan: Totally understandable. For Redwood we support three main modes: hosted API (our managed), dedicated reserved capacity you can lease and resell, and private control plane for VPC/on-prem customers. We can support marketplace listings too.
[02:05] Irene Cho: For private control plane — can you confirm if we can manage networking on our side? We need VPC peering, private subnets, and we have strict egress controls.
[02:18] Samir Patel: Yes, private deployment supports VPC peering and customer-managed networking. There are also options for on-prem packages. We do need to align on KMS/HSM integration for key material.
[02:30] Irene Cho: KMS integration is mandatory for many customers. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-kms)?
[02:38] Alex Morgan: Yes, we support BYO KMS and HSM integrations, and can provide audit logs for model requests. We'll share our security docs.
[02:48] Rachel Lee: Great, security is table stakes. Also curious about pricing and unit economics — how do you handle batching/kv cache? Our customers are cost sensitive.
[03:05] Samir Patel: We have batching, prefix and KV cache to reduce per token cost. The Optimize toolkit recommends batching policies and quantization profiles by workload. For resale we can model the unit economics and provide a price sheet sample.
[03:20] Marco Diaz: Any concerns around model licensing if we resell capacity with certain open models?
[03:27] Alex Morgan: Model licensing is critical — for curated open models we verify performance and licensing. For some third-party licensed models, we require specific agreements. We'll flag that in the commercial sheet.
[03:40] Irene Cho: On the tech integration side, what's the typical onboarding footprint? e.g., how many hours for connectivity and a small benchmark?
[03:50] Samir Patel: For a pilot, typical onboarding is 1-2 weeks: network setup, auth/SSO, KMS setup, then run a small benchmark with 1-2 representative workloads. If you want to do dedicated GPU pools we add provision time which depends on capacity.
[04:06] Rachel Lee: For capacity, we want to know latency SLOs, throughput per GPU type, and how Redwood handles fallbacks if a region is constrained.
[04:18] Samir Patel: We support routing policies by latency/cost/region and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. We can provide per-GPU throughput profiles.
[04:30] Marco Diaz: Competitors — are there reasons customers come to Redwood vs Paperspace or Lambda?
[04:38] Alex Morgan: Two main differentiators: production-first runtime (latency and predictable throughput) and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private. Also cost controls and observability for rollouts and regressions.
[04:55] Irene Cho: Any pre-built connectors for common infra — e.g., Terraform modules, helm charts for private?
[05:02] Samir Patel: Yes we have terraform modules and helm charts for private deployments, plus scripts for autoscaling policies. We'll share the repo links.
[05:12] Rachel Lee: That's helpful. On legal/compliance, we need SOC2 type II evidence and a copy of your MSA redlines for partner resale.
[05:22] Alex Morgan: We can share SOC2 report after an NDA and our partner MSA draft; we'll include a sample reseller addendum.
[05:30] Marco Diaz: Pilot commercial model — are you able to do a co-sell/pilot credits model? Some vendors provide credits to lower friction.
[05:38] Alex Morgan: Yes, for partner pilots we often provide credits or discounted pilot pricing. For reseller models we can also do commit-based pricing for Dedicated.
[05:48] Irene Cho: Technical Q: how does Redwood handle KV cache persistence and warm starts across requests? Important for our latency-sensitive apps.
[05:58] Samir Patel: We manage KV cache in-memory for hot prefixes and can persist cold keys to local SSDs depending on deployment. There's an option for cross-request caching if you have sticky sessions; otherwise we recommend prefix caching. We'll include a tech note.
[06:15] Rachel Lee: Sounds good. What would success look like for Nimbus on a 90-day timeline?
[06:22] Marco Diaz: For us success is: (1) pilot demonstrating throughput and latency on H100 for a standard convo app, (2) commercial terms agreed for reseller pilot, (3) security checklist completed.
[06:33] Alex Morgan: That aligns. Proposed next steps: share partner deck and security docs, schedule pilot kickoff, and align on commercial model.
[06:42] Irene Cho: On pilot workload — we'll define two benchmarks: chat (real-time low latency) and batch embeddings. We can provide sample data and expected QPS.
[06:53] Samir Patel: Perfect, we'll prepare a benchmark checklist and perf spreadsheet.
[07:00] Rachel Lee: Any blockers from Redwood side we should be aware of?
[07:06] Alex Morgan: None immediate; main things are getting the security questionnaire and network access in place. Also we might need minor contract work for reseller language.
[07:18] Marco Diaz: On the marketplace listing route — will Redwood support a listing in Nimbus' marketplace with single-sign-on?
[07:26] Samir Patel: We have marketplace integrations and can surface products via API. SSO for provisioning can be integrated; we'll need to work through provisioning APIs and billing reconciliation.
[07:39] Irene Cho: Billing reconciliation is a pain point — we need clear metering and usage exports.
[07:44] Alex Morgan: Redwood provides token-level usage exports and per-route/model dashboards; we can set retention and export intervals.
[07:56] Rachel Lee: Good. Can you share an example dashboard or CSV export so our finance team can model payouts?
[08:04] Samir Patel: Yep, we'll attach a sample usage export and billing report template.
[08:12] Marco Diaz: On support SLAs, do partners get a tiered SLA or white-glove support for reseller accounts?
[08:20] Alex Morgan: Partners can opt into premium support tiers with faster response times and dedicated CSMs for enterprise reseller programs. We'll include support tiers in the partner deck.
[08:33] Irene Cho: A quick nit: we have customers needing in-region data residency in EU and APAC; do you have regional control and on-prem packaging?
[08:45] Samir Patel: Yes we have regional deployments and an on-prem package for heavily regulated customers. We'll list region availability and timelines.
[08:56] Rachel Lee: Perfect. Any technical demo we should run for the pilot?
[09:02] Samir Patel: Typical demo: run an H100 chat model test, measure p99 latency and throughput, then run embedding batch. We'll coordinate test vectors.
[09:14] Marco Diaz: When can we get the commercial one-pager and sample MSA?
[09:18] Alex Morgan: We'll send the one-pager and sample MSA by EOD Friday, 2026-04-02.
[09:26] Irene Cho: Can Samir send the integration docs and terraform repo links?
[09:30] Samir Patel: I'll send the links and a short onboarding checklist by Monday 2026-04-03.
[09:36] Rachel Lee: Legal will want to review SOC2 — do you need an NDA?
[09:40] Alex Morgan: We typically exchange an NDA; I'll loop legal and send a one-way NDA so you can get SOC2.
[09:48] Marco Diaz: Sounds good. Any closing questions?
[09:52] Irene Cho: One more: do you support GPU telemetry for our ops team to manage autoscaling?
[09:58] Samir Patel: Yes, we emit telemetry and metrics for GPU utilization, queue lengths, and latencies; integrates with Prometheus/Grafana.
[10:08] Rachel Lee: OK great. Let's recap next steps, and we'll circle back after we get the security questionnaire into you.
[10:16] Alex Morgan: Recap: Alex sends partner deck + MSA draft; Samir sends tech docs, terraform, perf checklist; Irene fills security questionnaire; schedule pilot week of 4/13.
[10:28] Marco Diaz: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[10:32] Alex Morgan: Thanks all.

Notes: Transcript has light recognition errors in some technical terms (K-V cash noted in transcript as K-V cash in one pass), timer stamps are periodic. Shared artifacts referenced: partner_deck_v1.pdf (will be sent), security_questionnaire.xlsx (to be filled), perf_spreadsheet.csv (will be attached).
